components.name: Support-Session Confirmation
components.description: App-scoped admin confirmation that identifies the represented user, scope, duration, audit reason, and mutability before authority is granted.
components.html:
Start a support session

You’ll enter one app as alice for up to 15 minutes. A persistent banner identifies you as the administrator.

Stored in the audit log. Be specific enough for another administrator to understand later.

This is not read-only. Actions inside the app can change the user’s data. The session cannot access ShinyHub’s admin dashboard, other apps, API tokens, or privileged users.

components.name: Persistent Support-Session Rail
components.description: Platform-owned cross-world safety rail that continuously exposes actor, subject, mutability, deadline, and exit.
components.html:
Support session · Viewing as alice
admin is the administrator. Actions here can change alice’s data.
Ends in 14:27
components.css: .ds-support-rail { min-height: 52px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; padding: 8px clamp(12px,2vw,24px); color: #FFF8E7; background: #21170A; border-bottom: 1px solid #A86608; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(15,9,2,.28); font: 600 14px/1.35 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-support-mark { width: 28px; height: 28px; flex: 0 0 auto; color: #FBBF24; } .ds-support-copy { min-width: 0; flex: 1 1 auto; } .ds-support-title { font-weight: 760; letter-spacing: -.012em; } .ds-support-detail { margin-top: 1px; color: #F7DCA3; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 520; } .ds-support-timer { white-space: nowrap; color: #FFE9B8; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 12px; } .ds-support-rail button { appearance: none; border: 1px solid #F59E0B; border-radius: 8px; padding: 7px 11px; background: #F59E0B; color: #241604; font: 750 12px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-support-rail button:hover { background: #FBBF24; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(245,158,11,.22); } .ds-support-rail button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #FFF8E7; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-support-rail button:disabled { cursor: wait; opacity: .66; box-shadow: none; } @media (max-width:620px) { .ds-support-rail { align-items: flex-start; gap: 9px; padding: 9px 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-support-mark { width: 24px; height: 24px; } .ds-support-copy { flex-basis: calc(100% - 36px); } .ds-support-timer { margin-left: 33px; } .ds-support-rail button { margin-left: auto; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-support-rail button { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview: Temporary security states remain native to Constellation inside the admin workflow. When that state crosses into arbitrary app content, one persistent amber safety rail carries the platform boundary with it: the rail names who is acting, who is represented, whether actions can mutate data, when authority ends, and how to exit.
keyCharacteristics: One unmistakable amber rail for temporary cross-world security states.

rules.name: The Amber Safety-State Rule
rules.body: Use the full amber treatment only for an active security or safety boundary with an explicit consequence and exit. Keep the host application visually untouched so the rail remains the single unmistakable platform signal.

rules.name: The Cross-World Boundary Rule
rules.body: Platform safety chrome owns its own layout and must remain legible across arbitrary app themes, frameworks, and responsive behavior.

rules.name: The Pending Means Committed Rule
rules.body: Once a security-sensitive action is in flight, the modal cannot imply cancellation by disappearing while the request may still succeed.

rules.name: The No Invisible Identity Switch Rule
rules.body: A represented session is never communicated by account data alone; the persistent rail must continuously expose actor, subject, mutability, deadline, and exit.

dos: Do use actor, subject, and mutability as separate concepts whenever authority is temporarily represented.
Do keep security-sensitive confirmation dialogs open and visibly busy while their request is pending.
Do keep countdowns visually precise but announce only meaningful time thresholds to assistive technology.
Do mount cross-world safety chrome at the document boundary and make it self-heal after hosted-app DOM replacement.
donts: Don't let a hosted app inherit, reposition, dismiss, or visually absorb platform safety chrome.
Don't hide or truncate actor, subject, mutability, deadline, or exit when the safety rail wraps on mobile.
Don't announce a per-second countdown through a live region or allow a pending support-session request to be dismissed.
